title: Sliding-window Commit Allocator and Isolation Tethering - PRD idea
summary: Sketch for a time-windowed commit allocator that smooths tenant burst behavior while preserving isolation guarantees. Introduces 'isolation tethering' — a lightweight binding between transient burst credit and reserved capacity to reduce noisy-neighbor regressions during high concurrency.
problem_statement: Current dedicated pool autoscalers either rigidly reserve capacity (wasted headroom) or over-index on opportunistic bursting (noisy neighbors). Tenants that briefly spike can cause tail latency regressions for co-tenants. We need a mechanism that: 1) lets tenants burst predictably without overprovisioning, 2) enforces stronger soft-isolation during contention, and 3) can be rolled back or dialed down automatically when regressions are detected.
goals: Enable short-lived bursts for tenants without requiring long-term reserved capacity
Limit cross-tenant performance degradation during contention windows
Provide observable, auditable rules tying bursts to tenant commitments
Allow automated rollback/mitigation when SLO regressions are detected
non_goals: Solve price/modeling for every workload pattern (focus is operational control)
Guarantee zero-impact bursts under extreme oversubscription
proposal_overview: Introduce a sliding-window commit allocator (SWCA) that tracks per-tenant commit usage in fixed-length windows (e.g., 5m windows with 1m slide). Tenants have base reserved units + a burst credit allowance that accrues slowly and decays within the window. When a tenant consumes burst credits, an 'isolation tether' is created that pins a small fraction of reserved headroom to that tenant for the remainder of the window (tether multiplier). Tethers reduce the effective opportunistic pool available to others, providing soft isolation. SWCA exposes adjustable knobs (window length, tether multiplier, accrual rate, max burst cap) and integrates with rollback hedges that trigger automatic throttles or model fallbacks if cluster-level latency SLOs worsen.
design_primitives: windowed-usage-buckets: circular buffers of commit counts per tenant
burst-accrual: linear or exponential accrual models configurable per tenant profile
iso-tether: ephemeral reservation token that deducts a percentage of headroom from shared pool
rollback-hedge: auto-fallback policy that reduces burst caps or shifts traffic to lower-fidelity model variants
telemetry-hooks: per-tenant and per-pool latency/queue-depth traces for detection
api_surface: Admin endpoints and console controls: 1) POST /tenants/{id}/burst-config {accrual_rate, max_burst_tokens, tether_multiplier, window_length}, 2) GET /tenants/{id}/window-usage, 3) GET /pools/{id}/iso-map, 4) operator endpoints: POST /pools/{id}/trigger-rollback, 5) telemetry streaming for per-window metrics. SDKs surface light-weight client hints: preferBurst=true, burstPriority=[low|normal|high].
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal sim run (1-2 weeks) against recorded traces. Phase 1: limited opt-in beta for a small set of tenants (non-critical) with conservative defaults (short windows, low tether multiplier). Phase 2: enable telemetry-driven automatic hedges with rollback turned on for beta tenants. Phase 3: broader availability with dashboard and per-tenant tuning. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria (see metrics).
ops_playbook: When cluster tail latency > target for 3 sliding windows: 1) Automated: reduce global max_burst_tokens by 25% and increase tether_multiplier by 0.2; 2) If latency persists: trigger rollback for top contributors, redirecting traffic to fallback model; 3) Alert SRE and product: produce post-mortem including iso-map snapshots and top-k tenant usage. Maintain a runbook with commands and playbook links for manual override.
metrics: iso-tether coverage (percentage of headroom currently tethered)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Tethers can reduce overall utilization. Mitigation: conservative tether multiplier defaults and dynamic decay when pool under-utilized.
Risk: Gaming by tenants (intentional spike to secure headroom). Mitigation: reputational throttles, burst billing, and anomaly detectors.
Risk: Complexity in telemetry and false positives triggering rollback. Mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation (latency + queue depth + error rate) before automated rollback.
Risk: Operational confusion with many knobs. Mitigation: provide sensible presets (developer, production, high-isolation) and UI guidance.
open_questions: Best default window length for mixed workloads? (5m vs 1m vs 30s)
How to surface per-tenant economic signals (billing) when bursts are used?
Operator UX: should rollback be reversible automatically or require human ack?
Interaction with existing warm pools and prewarming: can tethers be momentarily borrowed from warm-pools?
